verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 launch is scheduled for 6:35 p.m. ET on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'lifted off from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R7: 'Liftoff occurred at 6:35 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm the exact scheduled and actual liftoff time of 6:35 p.m. ET on April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 launch is from Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'lift off from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R4: 'Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B'; R3: 'Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources explicitly state the launch is from Kennedy Space Center.

verifications.claim: Live coverage of the Artemis 2 launch is available via NASA's YouTube channel.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA is also broadcasting the launch attempt live on its YouTube channel'; R6: 'NASA official broadcast (YouTube and NASA+)'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm live coverage on NASA's YouTube channel.

verifications.claim: Live coverage of the Artemis 2 launch is available via NASA+ streaming service.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: R6 explicitly mentions live coverage on NASA+.

verifications.claim: Live coverage of the Artemis 2 launch is available via the NASA website NASA.gov.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.reasoning: R4 is a NASA.gov blog with live launch day updates, but not explicitly 'live coverage' like video streaming; broader than precise video stream.

verifications.claim: News coverage of the Artemis 2 launch is available on CBS News 24/7.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R8: 'CBS News' streaming channel, CBS News 24/7, will have coverage throughout the day'
verifications.reasoning: R8 directly states CBS News 24/7 provides coverage.

verifications.claim: News coverage of the Artemis 2 launch is available on NBC News NOW.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'tune into ​​​​​NBC News NOW'; R7: 'NBC News NOW'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm NBC News NOW coverage.

verifications.claim: News coverage of the Artemis 2 launch is available on FOX Weather YouTube.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No references mention FOX Weather YouTube coverage.

verifications.claim: News coverage of the Artemis 2 launch is available on ABC News/National Geographic.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No direct mention of live news coverage from ABC News or National Geographic; post-launch video in R2 but not news coverage.

verifications.claim: Spanish coverage of the Artemis 2 launch is available on NASA's Spanish YouTube channel.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No references mention Spanish coverage or NASA's Spanish YouTube channel.

verifications.claim: NASA will stream live views from the Orion spacecraft after the Artemis 2 launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: 'NASA plans to continue broadcasting live views of the Artemis II mission'; R2: live feeds from Orion
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm NASA streams live views from Orion post-launch.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will make a 10-day journey around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'return in 10 days'; R2: 'nearly 10-day journey around the moon'; R3: 'approximately 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state a 10-day mission around the moon.

verifications.claim: Tickets for viewing the Artemis 2 launch at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex are available.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Main Visitor Complex Launch Viewing Package SOLD OUT'; 'Feel the Heat Launch Viewing Package (Limited Quantities) SOLD OUT'
verifications.reasoning: R3 explicitly states viewing packages are sold out, contradicting availability.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 launch is expected to be visible in the sky across a large part of Florida and southeast Georgia.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: 'visibility range for when people may be able to see the launch... across most of Florida'; R8: 'across most of Florida and southeastern Georgia'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm visibility across large parts of Florida and southeast Georgia.
